questions.stem: An emergency department triage nurse uses the Emergency Severity Index (ESI). Which client should be assigned ESI level 1?

options.text: A client with an ankle injury who can't bear weight
A client with chest pain who is pale and diaphoretic, with a blood pressure of 78/40 mm Hg
A client with abdominal pain who needs labs and a CT scan, with normal vital signs
A client who needs a prescription refill

rationale.correct: ESI 1 means immediate life-saving intervention is needed: unstable airway, breathing or circulation.

perOption.a: Stable, needs one resource (x-ray): ESI 4.
perOption.b: ESI 1 is for clients who need immediate life-saving intervention.
perOption.c: Needs two or more resources but is stable: ESI 3.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: A clinic nurse is returning phone calls. Which caller should the nurse advise to call 911?

options.text: A client with a sore throat and a temperature of 38.1 °C (100.6 °F)
A client who suddenly can't lift the right arm and has slurred speech that began 20 minutes ago
A client with diabetes whose glucose is 210 mg/dL
A client asking whether to take ibuprofen for back pain

rationale.correct: Signs of stroke need emergency medical services: time to treatment determines outcome.

perOption.a: Can be seen in the clinic or urgent care.
perOption.b: Sudden weakness and slurred speech suggest stroke; emergency transport saves time.
perOption.c: Needs advice and follow-up, not an emergency.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: A home health nurse plans visits for the day. Which client should the nurse visit first?

options.text: A client with a stage 2 pressure injury who needs a weekly dressing change
A client on warfarin who called saying their gums have been bleeding since this morning
A client with stable COPD due for a monthly assessment
A client who needs teaching about a new glucometer

rationale.correct: Visit first the client with a possible unstable or worsening condition.

perOption.a: Routine wound care can be scheduled later.
perOption.b: Active bleeding on an anticoagulant may signal a high INR and needs prompt assessment.
perOption.d: Teaching can be scheduled later in the day.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: In a long-term care facility, which resident should the nurse assess first?

options.text: A resident with dementia who is wandering in the hallway
A resident who has new confusion and a temperature of 38.4 °C (101.1 °F) this morning
A resident who refused breakfast
A resident who wants to call family

rationale.correct: An acute change from baseline in an older adult needs prompt assessment.

perOption.a: Needs supervision, but the behavior is usual for this resident.
perOption.b: An acute change in mental status with fever suggests infection or sepsis in an older adult.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: In the intensive care unit, which client needs the nurse's attention first?

options.text: A client on a ventilator whose high-pressure alarm sounds while coughing
A client with an arterial line whose waveform has become dampened
A client whose cardiac monitor shows ventricular fibrillation
A client receiving a sedative infusion who opens eyes to voice

rationale.correct: A lethal rhythm needs immediate action.

perOption.a: Coughing commonly triggers the alarm; it settles when the cough stops.
perOption.b: Needs troubleshooting soon, but a dampened waveform alone isn't life-threatening.
perOption.c: Ventricular fibrillation is cardiac arrest; immediate defibrillation is needed.
perOption.d: Light sedation is often the goal.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: The charge nurse reviews the unit board at 07:30. Highlight the client situations that need the charge nurse's attention first.

cells: Client 1 day after a hysterectomy; pain 4/10 after oral analgesic
Client with pneumonia; SpO2 dropped from 95% to 87%, now restless
Client awaiting discharge; ride arrives at 11:00
Client on heparin infusion; aPTT 140 seconds (target 60-85)
Client with diabetes; breakfast glucose 178 mg/dL
Client with hip fracture; new pallor and pulselessness of the foot

rationale.correct: Act on new hypoxemia, a dangerous anticoagulation level and loss of circulation before stable findings.

perOption.r2: Acute hypoxemia with restlessness needs immediate assessment.
perOption.r4: Supratherapeutic aPTT puts the client at risk of bleeding; the infusion must be adjusted per protocol.
perOption.r5: Treat per sliding scale; not urgent.
perOption.r6: Signs of arterial compromise need emergency action.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize the most urgent situations on a unit.

questions.stem: The nurse receives these four calls at the start of the shift. Place them in the order the nurse should respond, from first to last.

items.text: A client receiving a blood transfusion reports chills and back pain
A client with diabetes reports feeling shaky and sweaty
A client 30 minutes after a thoracentesis reports sudden shortness of breath
A client asks for help to the bathroom

rationale.correct: Breathing first, then an acute transfusion reaction, then hypoglycemia, then routine needs.

perOption.a: Possible pneumothorax: an airway and breathing emergency.
perOption.b: Possible hemolytic reaction: the transfusion must be stopped right away.
perOption.c: Likely hypoglycemia: treat promptly, but the first two are more immediately life-threatening.
perOption.d: Safety need, but it can be delegated or met after the urgent calls.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a client who just returned from surgery. Which finding requires the nurse's immediate action?

options.text: Pain rated 5 out of 10
Snoring respirations with SpO2 of 86%
Urine output 40 mL in the last hour
Small amount of serosanguineous drainage on the dressing

rationale.correct: An obstructed airway after anesthesia is the priority.

perOption.a: Needs treatment, but not the most urgent.
perOption.b: Snoring after anesthesia suggests a partially obstructed airway; reposition and support the airway now.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: The RN on a rehabilitation unit is delegating tasks. For each task, indicate whether it can be delegated to assistive personnel (AP).

rows.text: Helping a stable client with range-of-motion exercises taught by the therapist
Checking a client's blood glucose with a meter, if trained and allowed by policy
Deciding whether a client is ready to walk without assistance
Feeding a client with a new swallowing disorder

rationale.correct: AP may perform routine, standardized tasks for stable clients; the RN keeps assessment, judgment and care of unstable clients.

perOption.r1:c1: Routine, standardized task for a stable client.
perOption.r2:c1: Point-of-care glucose checks are delegable to trained AP in many facilities; the RN interprets the result.
perOption.r2:c2: Delegable when trained and allowed by policy.
perOption.r3:c2: Assessment and evaluation can't be delegated.
perOption.r4:c1: The client is unstable for feeding; aspiration risk needs licensed assessment.
perOption.r4:c2: A new dysphagia needs licensed staff until a plan is established.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Decide which tasks to delegate on a rehabilitation unit.

questions.stem: A nurse from a staffing agency is new to the unit. Which assignment is most appropriate?

options.text: A client receiving a first dose of chemotherapy
Two stable clients recovering from routine surgery
Charge nurse for the shift
A client with a new tracheostomy and frequent suctioning needs

rationale.correct: Give new or agency staff stable clients with predictable care.

perOption.a: Needs a nurse familiar with the unit's protocols and the client's plan.
perOption.b: Stable clients with predictable care are appropriate for staff new to the unit.
perOption.c: Requires knowledge of the unit, its staff and resources.
perOption.d: High-acuity care should go to experienced unit staff.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Make safe assignments for agency staff.

questions.stem: The RN is working with an LPN in a long-term care facility. Select the 3 tasks that are appropriate for the RN to assign to the LPN.

options.text: Giving scheduled insulin to a resident with stable diabetes
Performing a sterile dressing change on a healing wound
Reinforcing fall-prevention teaching the RN started
Doing the admission assessment on a new resident
Developing the plan of care for a resident with a new pressure injury
Evaluating a resident's response to a new pain management plan

rationale.correct: LPNs give medications and treatments to stable clients and reinforce teaching; RNs assess, plan and evaluate.

perOption.a: Medication administration to stable residents is within LPN scope.
perOption.b: Wound care for stable residents is within LPN scope.
perOption.d: Initial assessment is an RN responsibility.
perOption.e: Care planning is an RN responsibility.
perOption.f: Evaluation of the plan is an RN responsibility.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Assign tasks to an LPN in long-term care.

questions.stem: A nurse almost gave a medication to the wrong client but caught the error during barcode scanning. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Nothing, because no harm occurred
Report the near miss through the facility's incident reporting system
Document the near miss in the client's medical record
Tell the client about the near miss and ask them to report it

rationale.correct: Near misses are reported to support a culture of safety.

perOption.a: Near misses are reported so the system can be fixed.
perOption.b: Near-miss reports help find system problems before someone is harmed.
perOption.c: Incident reports are not part of the medical record.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which statements about incident reports are accurate? Select all that apply.

options.text: They are completed for events that did or could have caused harm
They are filed in the client's medical record
They describe facts without blaming anyone
The nurse writes "incident report filed" in the nurse's notes
They are used to find patterns and improve safety
They are completed by the person who saw or was involved in the event

rationale.correct: Incident reports are factual, separate from the chart, and used for quality improvement.

perOption.a: Includes near misses and actual events.
perOption.b: They are kept separately from the medical record.
perOption.d: The medical record shouldn't reference the incident report.
perOption.e: Quality improvement relies on reporting data.
perOption.f: The person with first-hand knowledge files the report.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: A unit has had three client falls in a month, all at night. What is the best first step for the quality improvement team?

options.text: Discipline the nurses on duty
Gather data about the falls, such as times, causes and contributing factors
Restrain all high-risk clients at night
Stop admitting older adults to the unit

rationale.correct: QI begins by collecting and analyzing data to find causes.

perOption.a: Blame doesn't fix system problems.
perOption.b: Analyzing data reveals patterns and root causes.
perOption.c: Restraints increase injury risk and aren't a first-line fix.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client died after receiving the wrong blood type. What type of event is this, and what review is required?

options.text: A near miss requiring no review
A sentinel event requiring a root cause analysis
An expected complication requiring only documentation
A minor event requiring a staff meeting

rationale.correct: Sentinel events need a root cause analysis focused on systems, not blame.

perOption.a: Harm occurred; this isn't a near miss.
perOption.b: Unexpected death or serious harm is a sentinel event; a root cause analysis looks for system causes.
perOption.c: Wrong-type transfusion is a preventable error, not an expected complication.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence about safety culture.

content.template: In a just culture, a nurse who made an honest mistake is {{b1}}, while a nurse who knowingly skipped a required safety check is {{b2}}.

options.text: supported, and the system is examined
fired right away
ignored
held accountable for reckless behavior
treated exactly the same as an honest mistake
rewarded for saving time

rationale.correct: Just culture: console human error, coach at-risk behavior, and hold reckless behavior accountable.

perOption.b1:a: Human error is addressed by improving systems.
perOption.b2:a: Conscious disregard of safety rules calls for accountability.
perOption.b2:b: Just culture separates error from reckless behavior.
perOption.b2:c: Skipping safety checks puts clients at risk.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: The unit's catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI) rate has risen. Which change would most likely reduce it?

options.text: Changing all catheters every 3 days
A nurse-driven protocol to remove catheters when criteria are no longer met
Adding antibiotics for all clients with catheters
Irrigating catheters daily

rationale.correct: Catheter days drive CAUTI; nurse-driven removal protocols lower rates.

perOption.a: Routine changes aren't recommended.
perOption.b: Removing catheters as early as possible is the most effective prevention.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: Two nurses are arguing loudly at the nurses' station about a shared assignment. What should the charge nurse do first?

options.text: Tell them to stop and discuss it later
Move the discussion to a private area and listen to both nurses
Report both nurses to the manager
Decide who is right and reassign the work

rationale.correct: Address conflict promptly, privately and with both parties heard.

perOption.a: Avoids the conflict without resolving it.
perOption.b: Privacy and listening to both sides support resolution.
perOption.c: Escalation may be needed later, but first try to resolve it.
perOption.d: Deciding without hearing both sides is unfair.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: A new graduate tells the charge nurse that an experienced nurse often makes belittling comments in front of others. What should the charge nurse do?

options.text: Tell the new graduate to toughen up
Take the report seriously and follow the facility's policy for addressing incivility
Confront the experienced nurse in front of the team
Change the new graduate's schedule so they never work together

rationale.correct: Incivility and bullying are safety issues and must be addressed.

perOption.a: Dismisses lateral violence, which harms safety and retention.
perOption.b: Lateral violence is addressed through policy and leadership.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: A nurse is assigned more clients than they believe they can safely care for. What should the nurse do first?

options.text: Refuse the assignment and leave the unit
Accept the assignment and tell no one
Discuss the concerns with the charge nurse and ask for help or a change
Call the state board of nursing

rationale.correct: Voice safety concerns about assignments through the chain of command.

perOption.a: Leaving after accepting report may be client abandonment.
perOption.b: Unsafe staffing needs to be raised.
perOption.c: Raise concerns through the chain of command; document per policy (for example, an assignment despite objection form).

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: The nurse manager is planning a change to a new documentation system. Which strategy best reduces staff resistance?

options.text: Announce the change one day before go-live
Involve staff early, explain why the change is needed and provide training
Require staff to learn the system on their own time
Avoid answering questions about the change

rationale.correct: Change management: involve staff, explain the reason, and support learning.

perOption.a: Short notice increases resistance.
perOption.b: Participation and understanding reduce resistance to change.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: A nursing student asks to give a medication the student has not given before. The nurse is the student's preceptor today. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Let the student give it alone to build confidence
Review the medication with the student and supervise the administration
Refuse to let the student give any medications
Give the medication and have the student document it

rationale.correct: Supervise students when they perform new skills.

perOption.a: The student needs supervision with new skills.
perOption.b: Supervision keeps the client safe while the student learns.
perOption.d: Students shouldn't document care they didn't give.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client with heart failure has been readmitted three times in 2 months. Which referral is most likely to reduce readmissions?

options.text: Case management for transitional care and follow-up
Psychiatric consultation
Speech therapy
Chaplain visit

rationale.correct: Case management coordinates care across settings for high-risk clients.

perOption.a: Case managers coordinate follow-up, medications and home support.
perOption.b: Not indicated by the information given.
perOption.d: Supportive, but doesn't address the readmission causes.

questions.stem: A client without insurance needs ongoing diabetes supplies after discharge. Which team member should the nurse contact?

options.text: Social worker
Physical therapist
Respiratory therapist
Dietitian

rationale.correct: Social workers help with financial barriers and community resources.

perOption.a: Social workers connect clients with financial and community resources.
perOption.b: Not related to supplies.
perOption.d: Helps with diet, not resources for supplies.

questions.stem: A client is being transferred to a skilled nursing facility. Which action is most important for continuity of care?

options.text: Give a verbal or written report to the receiving nurse, including medications and recent changes
Send the client with a list of hospital phone numbers only
Tell the family to explain the client's care
Transfer without a report because the chart is available online

rationale.correct: Transitions of care require a complete handoff, including medication reconciliation.

perOption.a: A complete handoff prevents errors at transitions.
perOption.b: Not enough information.
perOption.c: The nurse is responsible for handoff.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment

questions.stem: The nurse is completing medication reconciliation at discharge. Which actions are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: Compare home medications with the hospital medications
Ask about over-the-counter drugs and supplements
Give the client an updated, complete medication list
Assume home medications should all continue
Clarify any discrepancies with the provider
Skip reconciliation if the client takes fewer than three medications

rationale.correct: Medication reconciliation at every transition prevents errors.

perOption.a: Finds omissions and duplications.
perOption.b: These can interact with prescriptions.
perOption.c: Clients and the next providers need an accurate list.
perOption.d: Each must be reviewed for continuation.
perOption.e: Discrepancies must be resolved before discharge.
perOption.f: Reconciliation is done for every client.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: The hospital has one isolation room left and two clients need it. Which client should get the room?

options.text: A client with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis
A client with MRSA in a wound that is covered
Both should share the room
Neither, because isolation rooms are only for clients receiving chemotherapy

rationale.correct: Use scarce airborne isolation rooms for airborne infections.

perOption.a: Airborne infections require a negative-pressure isolation room.
perOption.b: Contact precautions can be done in a regular private room.
perOption.c: Clients with different infections shouldn't share a room.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment

questions.stem: The nurse is caring for four clients. For each client, select the priority action.

cells.text: Client receiving IV vancomycin with flushing and itching of the face and neck
Client 2 days after surgery with a red, swollen, tender calf
Client with a new prescription for an ACE inhibitor who has lip swelling

options.text: Slow the infusion and notify the provider
Speed up the infusion to finish sooner
Apply ice to the face
Keep the client in bed and notify the provider
Massage the calf
Encourage walking
Hold the medication and assess the airway
Give the next dose with food
Document as a minor side effect

rationale.correct: Recognize and act on adverse reactions and complications quickly.

perOption.b1:a: This is an infusion-rate reaction; slowing the infusion relieves it.
perOption.b1:b: A faster rate worsens the reaction.
perOption.b2:a: Suspected DVT: avoid moving the leg until evaluated.
perOption.b2:c: Not until a DVT is ruled out.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: The nurse is preparing for a busy shift. For each priority level, select the client who belongs there.

options.text: Client with a new irregular heart rate and dizziness
Client who needs a routine bath
Client waiting for transport to radiology
Client who needs help ordering lunch
Client with new chest pain
Client needing discharge teaching

rationale.correct: Urgent changes come first; routine tasks can be delegated.

perOption.a: New dysrhythmia with symptoms is urgent.
perOption.b: Not urgent.

questions.stem: Which action should the nurse take first when beginning the shift?

options.text: Review the assignment and get report on all clients
Start giving morning medications
Begin charting
Restock supplies

rationale.correct: Begin with report, then plan priorities.

perOption.a: Information first allows safe prioritization.
perOption.b: Report and prioritization come first.

questions.educationalObjective: Organize the start of a shift.

questions.stem: The nurse in a dialysis center is caring for four clients. Which client needs immediate attention?

options.text: A client who reports cramping in the legs during dialysis
A client whose potassium before dialysis was 5.6 mEq/L
A client who suddenly has chest pain, shortness of breath and coughing during dialysis
A client who wants to sleep during treatment

rationale.correct: Sudden chest pain and dyspnea during dialysis can mean a life-threatening complication such as air embolism.

perOption.a: Common; manage per protocol.
perOption.b: Dialysis will lower potassium.
perOption.c: These may signal an air embolism or another serious complication.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment

questions.stem: The RN observes assistive personnel (AP) taking a blood pressure. Which action by the AP requires the RN to intervene?

options.text: Using a cuff that covers about 80% of the arm's circumference
Taking the blood pressure on the arm with an IV infusing
Supporting the client's arm at heart level
Waiting 5 minutes after the client sits down

rationale.correct: Supervision includes correcting unsafe technique.

perOption.a: Correct cuff size.
perOption.b: Inflating a cuff over an IV can damage the vein and interrupt the infusion.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment

questions.stem: An assistive personnel (AP) refuses to help with a client on contact precautions, saying they are afraid of getting sick. What should the nurse do first?

options.text: Report the AP for refusing work
Explain how contact precautions and PPE protect staff, and offer to go in together
Do all the care for that client without discussing it
Ask the client to wait until another AP is available

rationale.correct: Address staff concerns with education and support.

perOption.a: Address the concern first.
perOption.b: Education and support address fear and maintain care.
